changes: original_meaning 保留拉丁语 speciosus 的 gloss「好看的，貌美的」（牛津同）。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明贬义的拉丁伏笔与英语里翻脸的确切年代（1610 年代，Etymonline 编年），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "specious (adj.) late 14c., \"pleasing to the sight, fair,\" from Latin speciosus \"good-looking, beautiful, fair,\" also \"showy, pretended, plausible, specious\"... from species \"appearance, form, figure, beauty\""
Etymonline: "Meaning \"seemingly desirable, reasonable or probable, but not really so; superficially fair, just, or correct\" in English is recorded from 1610s."
Oxford: "late Middle English (in the sense 'beautiful'): from Latin speciosus 'fair', from species 'appearance, form, beauty', from specere 'to look'."
specious.mechanism_sentence: specious 与 species 同家（都是「看」的亲戚），本义是「好看」：拉丁语里它已经兼着「装模作样的」一味，1610 年代在英语里彻底翻脸——长得像真的，正是问题所在。

semantic_path.how: 好看翻了脸（感情色彩贬化）：英语 14 世纪末入词时 specious 还是褒义的『悦目』；1610 年代新义落定——『看上去合情合理、其实站不住的』（Etymonline 编年）。表面的漂亮，从此成了不可信的证据。
semantic_path.meaning: 似是而非的，华而不实的

changes: original_meaning 按拉丁语 spectaculum 的 gloss 收为「公开的演出，展示」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年（14 世纪中公共演出与『引人注目之物』双义并存；眼镜义 14 世纪末）替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "spectacle (n.) mid-14c., \"public entertainment, specially prepared or arranged display,\" from Old French spectacle \"sight, spectacle, Roman games\" (13c.), from Latin spectaculum \"a public show, spectacle, place from which shows are seen,\" from spectare \"to view, watch, behold,\" frequentative form of specere \"to look at\""
Etymonline: "The sense of \"object of public contempt, derision or wonderment\" is from mid-14c. Also \"device for assisting or enhancing vision\" (late 14c.)"
spectacle.mechanism_sentence: spectacle 就是「摆给人看的场面」（spectare 是「一再看」）：14 世纪它指罗马竞技那样的公共演出，后来一切壮观的、引人围观的景象都归它——连「帮人看」的眼镜（spectacles）也是它生的。

semantic_path.how: 从舞台扩到一切『被众目围观的东西』：英语 14 世纪中入词时，既指安排好的公共演出，也指惹人注视、围观的对象（褒贬两可，出了洋相也是 spectacle）——词库今义『壮观的场面；景象』即此支。

changes: original_meaning 保留拉丁语 spectrum 的 gloss「影像，幻影」。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站（1610 年代幻影义入英语 → 1670 年代牛顿光谱 → 1936 年泛指范围），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "spectrum (n.) 1610s, \"apparition, phantom, specter,\" a sense now obsolete, from Latin spectrum (plural spectra) \"an appearance, image, apparition, specter,\" from specere \"to look at, view\""

Etymonline: "The meaning \"visible band showing the successive colors, formed from a beam of light passed through a prism\" is recorded from 1670s. The word was extended to the entire range of radiation wavelengths (including visible light) by 1888. The figurative sense of \"entire range\" of any thing is from 1936."
spectrum.mechanism_sentence: spectrum 在拉丁语里是「影像、幻影」：1670 年代牛顿借它命名棱镜分光的彩带；1936 年，它又泛指一切「从这一端到那一端」的连续范围。

semantic_path.how: 牛顿给了它一份新差事（专名化的术语借用）：1670 年代 spectrum 指白光穿过棱镜展开的彩色带，1888 年扩到包括不可见光在内的全部辐射波段——从鬼影，变成光排出的队列。
1936 年比喻义落定：任何『从一端连续铺到另一端的全程』都可称 spectrum（政治光谱、意见光谱）——光有全程，别的事物也有全程；词库『范围，幅度』即此。

changes: original_meaning 与拉丁语 spiritus 的 gloss 对齐为「呼吸，气息」（spirare『呼吸』的派生；拟声说按 de Vaan 口径只记入 disputes 类信息，不写入路径——现行 disputes 已登记该引文）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站（13 世纪中生命原理 → 14 世纪灵魂/幽灵群 → 1580 年代精神活力义），烈酒旁支在第三站 how 中一句带过。
evidence: Etymonline: "spirit (n.) mid-13c., \"life, the animating or vital principle in man and animals,\"... from Latin spiritus \"a breathing (of respiration, also of the wind), breath;\" also \"breath of a god,\" hence \"inspiration; breath of life,\" hence life itself... derivative of spirare \"to breathe\""

Etymonline: "The meaning \"supernatural immaterial creature; angel, demon; an apparition\" is attested from mid-14c. The word is attested by late 14c. as \"ghost, disembodied soul of a person\"... It is attested from 1580s in the metaphoric sense of \"animation, vitality,\" and by c. 1600 as \"frame of mind with which something is done,\" also \"mettle, vigor of mind, courage.\""
Etymonline: "From late 14c. in alchemy as \"volatile substance; distillate\"... the sense of which narrowed to \"strong alcoholic liquor\" by 1670s."
spirit.mechanism_sentence: spirit 是拉丁语的「一口气」（spirare 是「呼吸」）：气是生命在场的证据，于是它管灵魂、管幽灵；16 世纪末又收回人的身上，管起了精神与情绪。

semantic_path.how: 拉丁 spiritus 在圣经译本里对译希腊语 pneuma、希伯来语 ruah（都是『气、灵』）：英语 13 世纪中入词即指『赋予人、兽以生命的原理』，14 世纪『灵魂』『离体的鬼魂』诸义聚齐——人断气后剩下的那口『气』，就是灵。
从宇宙的灵收回到个人的精气神：14 世纪中已有『性情、心境』义，1580 年代添『生气、活力』，约 1600 年定型为『做事的心境与劲头』（in high spirits 情绪高涨）——词库『精神；情绪』即此；炼金术一支（易挥发物→1670 年代烈酒 spirits）是旁亲。
